payload.entry: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: migrate file_history::read_blobs and memory_history::causes::batched_diff_tree onto run_git_unchecked_with_stdin — both still write all of stdin before reading stdout (synchronous stdin risk / deadlock on large batches); protocol-specific parsing kept them out of git-runner. Later project_stats facets must use the new helper from their first implementation.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: sase-core just check clippy still fails on clean-base clippy 1.95 nonminimal_bool in project_onboarding/classify.rs:500 (untouched by git-runner) — already tracked by sase-1an and previously reproduced on sase-1ko.2; this phase introduced no new clippy lints after type aliases for stdin/stdout workers.

Hardened file_history runner: centralized argv construction scrubs GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES/GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_NAMESPACE and sets GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Added run_git_unchecked_with_stdin/run_git_checked_with_stdin with concurrent stdin writer + stdout drain, stdin close, timeout kill/reap/join, and IO-failure detection. Verified with just test -p sase_core file_history (46 passed) covering env scrub, over-pipe stdin and stdout, batch success, nonzero exit, truncation on zero exit, timeout+blocked writer, and early-exit BrokenPipe. sase tool run check is red only on pre-existing clippy 1.95 nonminimal_bool in project_onboarding/classify.rs (sase-1an). No --epic-symbol leftovers. Deferred read_blobs and batched_diff_tree migration as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP.

payload.entry: FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE COMPLETE: Reviewed every child note. The four Clippy proposals (sase-1m3.4.1.1 note 1, .2 note 2, .3 note 1, .4 note 1) are one existing issue, corroborated with +1 on sase-1an. At core be2bfbee, classify.rs:500-502 still contains the exact expression and was last changed by 98c3682f; no fresh compiler run was claimed. The legacy batch migration proposed by sase-1m3.4.1.2 note 1 is new ready medium bug task sase-1mb: unchanged read_blobs and batched_diff_tree both synchronously write before stdout reading. Independent protocol reproduction left both writers blocked after 750ms despite a 100ms per-loop deadline, unblocked by killing/reaping Git. Source snapshots file:explicit:e8cdcc93ea565e0cc650ad8d and file:explicit:8ed243df05c3e11469a2e8d8 are attached to that task. Same-type and all-type searches, last-week sweep, and active-epic scope review found no duplicate or causal owner; the parent expressly defers these pre-existing callers. No other child follow-up was proposed or declined. The parent-phase skipped decision-record proposal remains deliberately unimplemented under final stats_decision_record=no; no memory change or duplicate task was created. Copy these outcomes into the final close note.

LAND AUDIT — NOT READY TO CLOSE: Reviewed every note on phases .1-.4, both audited plans, actual Rust source and commits ac370734/b0cd62b9/855ed4c3/be2bfbee. Parent DECISIONS honored: no memory changes; Code/Runs/plans remain explicit unimplemented seams and no Python caller exists. Source findings: query.rs collect_portfolio_code skips later history rows after identity/common-dir coverage dedupe, losing divergent selected refs from portfolio totals; coverage also counts duplicate declared identities across clones. load_unique_sources shares whole WalkedSource values, leaking the first ref alias and issue.repo into later specs. All-unavailable Output/lifetime uses measured zero because count fields are nonnullable and empty rows always aggregate; failed walks are treated as partial measured histories. mod.rs contains context structs and impl rather than only facade declarations/re-exports. The manual benchmark resolves to sase-core, independently checked by resolving its candidate paths; .4 measured 1568 core commits, not the required sase history. These remain epic work, addressed by the validated medium tale sase_plan_project_stats_core_landing.md, whose final step performs this epic and parent-phase closeout without waiting for its own commit. Integration review: core intervening 305b7b80 adds proposed_with for the later plans facet; sase 7545e85abf provenance is already compatible with footer parsing; 7c6b32457b inventory is for the later loader; 315092afeb repairs the parent .1/.2 fixtures as parent notes confirm. Other post-start commits concern docs/checks/release/UI. Both reviewed checkouts are on master, with no extra local origin/master commits at audit time. Current epic-symbols is empty. No fresh Rust compiler/gate pass claimed during this static landing audit; the tale must test regressions, measure actual sase, run guarded just check, and verify symbols before closing. Follow-up triage is complete in the preceding note; do not duplicate sase-1an or sase-1mb.

Landing repairs for sase-1m3.4.1 are complete. No distinct tale child bead existed; this close covers the inherited epic after the four original phases (.1–.4) stayed closed.

Repairs in linked sase-core:
- Source metadata, history reuse, and coverage identity are separate. Query always SHA-unions non-failed selected code histories; coverage/measurement unique by repository identity (path when unresolved); history cache key remains identity+common-dir+tip. Specs keep their own ref names and issue.repo. Worst-health wins so spec order cannot hide a partial/unavailable clone.
- Output/lifetime counts are nullable. Wholly unavailable sources serialize JSON null with empty models; empty repos and empty ranges stay measured 0; mixed success keeps numeric subtotals. Failed walks (HistoryOutcome.failed) are unavailable, not partial-with-zeros; truncated walks with complete records stay unfailed.
- Facet types moved to project_stats/facet.rs; mod.rs is declarations and re-exports only.
- Equal-tip complete cache hits skip persist; persist updates the process memo instead of evicting it; complete outcomes are interned across queries. Sole-repo project aggregates reuse the repo measurement.
- Manual acceptance requires PROJECT_STATS_SASE_REPO (non-SASE_ prefix), validates the sase primary (src/sase + sase-core-revision.txt, rejects sase-core), and does not fall back.

Verification:
